newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence 127.1 in May -- Conf Board.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence 127.1 in May -- Conf Board.

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence surged almost nine points to 127.1 in May, a 28-year high, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.
The April consumer confidence index reading was 118.5, it said.
The present situation component jumped to 152.2 in May from a revised reading of 141.6 in April, it added.
Meanwhile, the expectations component of the index, which has proven to be a key measure of future business activity, reached 110.3 in May from a revised 103.2 in the previous month.

"Consumers are not only upbeat about the current state of business activity but believe the economy will continue to expand over the next six months, " said Lynn Franco, associate director of The Conference Board's Consumer Research Center.
Franco added that U.S. consumer projections are in line with most of the key economic indicators, which are signaling healthy growth and only modest inflation ahead.

Nearly 33 percent of Americans said current business conditions are "good," up from less than 32 percent in April, according to the Conference Board. The percentage of people who feel "jobs are plentiful" rose to nearly 36 percent in May from 31 percent in April, it said.

Additionally, almost 19 percent of U.S. consumers believe business conditions will improve over the next six months, up from 16 percent last month. And almost 18 percent see more jobs opening up, compared with 14.5 percent in April, the Conference Board said.

"The Conference Board's new compensation survey suggests that pay inflation will be subdued through both 1997 and 1998, with salary increases averaging 4.0 percent in all major industries," Franco added.
